title: From the Editor — A Shadow on the Glass
settingText: A road town in brutal daylight above, with a cool dark stair descending below street level into the Mirage Club. Use the contrast between white exterior glare and deep interior shadow. No character reveal and no readable signage.
summary: Art-directed opening editorial splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 3. Entice the reader, establish the live pressure and world feeling, and preserve the story page-one reveal.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ART-DIRECTED SPLASH. Use one cinematic illustration rather than sequential panels. Reserve a large, deliberately quiet field for the supplied editorial body copy. The illustration supports the text without depicting the next issue's reveal literally.

LETTERING LAYOUT. Treat the supplied CAPTION lines as designed editorial typography, not speech balloons: strong heading, readable body copy, generous leading and margins, and a prominent final hook line. Do not invent any additional text, logos, signage, credits or slogans.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Names are expensive in the Sunfields.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Some can get you a bed. Some can get you shot. Some come with debts that survived the people who earned them.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: So there are places where nobody asks.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Beneath one of the road towns, the Mirage Club has made an entire refuge out of that bargain: leave the world upstairs, leave your history with it, and let everybody be whoever they say they are.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: After the Last Drop and Cinder Basin, Brandon could use a place like that.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For once, nobody should care what his name is.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Should.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Welcome to the Mirage.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: — Jeff Hines

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Star Splitter Visions

title: Down from the Basin
summary: The trio travels from Cinder Basin to a road town, still hungry and uncertain about the preacher but not chasing an explanation at the expense of eating.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — LARGE WIDE road panel: pale Sunfields, a repaired rig moving toward a compact road town built around old physical masonry and dark structural remnants. Unforgiving sunlight, not mystical twin-sun effects or generic frontier signage. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: CAPTION: “The road out of Cinder Basin was long enough for the dust to settle. It did nothing for the questions.”  Eva: “We know he got there first. We don't know who he is.”

Panel 2 — TIGHT across Jessie's shoulder; she drives in goggles with hair tied in a messy high bun, Brandon beside her, Eva behind holding her worn notebook closed. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Jessie: “We've also been driving since breakfast.”  Brandon: “We should stop somewhere we can eat.”

Panel 3 — TALL street-level reveal. A busy but unglamorous road town: people repairing a step, unloading sacks, ducking the sun. Stairs descending below street level are visible beneath a shop-front with no invented signs. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Eva: “Another saloon?”  Jessie: “A club. Supposed to be quiet enough to sit down.”
Panel 4 — SMALL face-to-face inset on Brandon and Jessie by the rig, both tired. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Brandon: “Is that what you said about the Last Drop?”  Jessie: “I said they had water.”

title: No Names Below
summary: The stairs and their single established notice introduce the Mirage Club's rule through the visitors' ordinary reactions.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — TALL STAIRWELL view down narrow worn wooden steps to amber practical lamps and copper rail fittings. The only readable environmental sign, beside stairs, must say exactly NO NAMES BELOW. No other lettering, posters or faux text. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: SIGN: “NO NAMES BELOW”  CAPTION: “Below the street, the Mirage Club had one rule worth writing down.”

Panel 2 — MEDIUM halfway down stairs: Eva reads notice aloud to Jessie. Brandon is ahead, hat in hand, avoiding a low pipe. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Eva: “No names below?”  Jessie: “Don't demand anyone's real name. Most people can manage it.”

Panel 3 — LOW viewpoint at club doorway: an unbadged house attendant quietly waves in a woman wearing travel wraps without asking her name. Nothing ceremonial. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Attendant: “Evening. There's room by the mirrors.”  Woman: “Thank you.”
Panel 4 — NARROW final inset: Brandon peers toward small tables and food from the bottom stair. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Brandon: “That suits me.”

title: A Place to Stay Unasked
summary: Show the Mirage as an intimate functioning social place: old mirrors, oxidized copper, performer, patron disagreements and work continuing.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — LARGE WIDE downstairs geography: low stage at rear left, copper-edged bar at right, worn mirror wall opposite, small tables in between. A narrow side corridor reaches dressing rooms and the only staircase. Isabella performs at the stage during the last phrase of a song; no written lyrics. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: CAPTION: “People came to the Mirage to hear a song, find company, or be left alone. Sometimes all three.”

Panel 2 — TIGHT on Marta, middle-aged bartender with rolled sleeves and oxidized-copper jewelry, wiping water rings from a tabletop. Len, older stage musician in patched dark vest, shifts his stool as a performer finishes. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Marta: “Food's still on. Kitchen's running late, as usual.”  Jessie: “Three plates.”

Panel 3 — MEDIUM at small table: Brandon sits where he can see the stairs only because it is the available seat. Eva looks up toward the stage; Jessie sets down her goggles. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Eva: “People really don't ask names?”  Jessie: “Try it sometime.”

Panel 4 — SMALL stage-to-floor angle: Isabella, elegant in worn dark stage layers, acknowledges a tired patron before stepping off for a short interval. She has not noticed Brandon. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Len: “Another one after the break?”  Isabella: “If you can keep the old piano awake.”

title: The Woman at the Mirrors
summary: Isabella's working relationships and dignity are visible before recognition; she spots Brandon naturally across her own club.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — MEDIUM by stage: Isabella hands Len a water glass, asking a practical question; Marta replenishes cups at the bar behind. No melodramatic entrance. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Isabella: “Did you eat?”  Len: “Not since you asked ten minutes ago.”  Isabella: “Then you've had ten minutes to fix that.”

Panel 2 — CLOSE at Brandon's table: warm ordinary food has arrived. Brandon reaches for a spoon, Jessie checks on Eva's plate, Eva is watching the room rather than eating. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Jessie: “Eat first. Ask questions after.”  Eva: “I can do both.”

Panel 3 — TALL perspective from Isabella's position across dark wood tables: she finally sees Brandon in profile lifting his hat off the neighboring chair. Her hand stops on the back of Len's stool. Other people keep moving and chatting. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: CAPTION: “Isabella Torres knew the room well enough to notice a stranger.”
Panel 4 — TIGHT silent on Isabella's face: surprise becomes anger tangled with relief. This is her reaction, not proof of Brandon's past. NO LETTERING.

title: You Came Back
summary: Isabella approaches and identifies Brandon as Merritt. The room's responses demonstrate the violated social custom.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE strong diagonal through tables: Isabella crosses toward Brandon as Jessie stands beside their meal. Conversations carry on until Isabella is close enough to speak. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Isabella: “You came back.”

Panel 2 — MEDIUM three-shot: Brandon looks up from an untouched mouthful; Isabella sees his face clearly, but no mystical resemblance overlay appears. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Brandon: “I'm not Merritt.”  Isabella: “Don't stand there like you don't know me.”

Panel 3 — LARGE ambient reaction: Marta glances at the stairs, Len stops adjusting the piano, two patrons turn chairs away; one glances toward the NO NAMES BELOW notice which is visible at a distance but not newly repeated as readable background text. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Jessie: “He doesn't know anybody here.”  Eva: “I thought you weren't supposed to use names.”
Panel 4 — TIGHT on Isabella who has heard Eva and remains undeterred. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Isabella: “The rule can survive one name.”  Brandon: “Can I eat first?”

title: The Rule Was for Everyone
summary: Show patrons' different instincts about protecting the club versus allowing Isabella's grievance, through behavior not a rules debate.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE table-level composition: some patrons look away deliberately; a couple closer to Isabella shift nearer. Marta still serves a waiting customer, unwilling to turn the place into a spectacle. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Marta: “Isabella.”  Isabella: “I know what I said.”

Panel 2 — MEDIUM near bar: Len quietly approaches, carrying the stool from the stage, not taking command. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Len: “People come here because we leave them be.”  Isabella: “People stayed here when Merritt walked away, too.”

Panel 3 — NARROW reaction at Brandon's table: Eva starts to speak but Jessie rests a hand on the edge of her chair, just enough to ask her to wait. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Eva: “Maybe she should—”  Jessie: “Give her a moment.”

Panel 4 — LOW close on Brandon putting his spoon down untouched. Isabella does not look triumphant. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: CAPTION: “For one name, the room had made room for a thousand different memories.”

title: Chains on the Doors
summary: Isabella begins telling Brandon what she remembers about Merritt during the club's old crackdown. This is her testimony, not a factual proof of Brandon's identity.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — LARGE intimate two-shot across a copper-edged table. Stage at rear falls into soft activity, not darkness; Isabella keeps herself controlled as she speaks. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Isabella: “When they chained the doors, you weren't there.”  Brandon: “I wasn't here.”

Panel 2 — CLOSE Isabella's hand on the tabletop, fingertips pressed flat. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Isabella: “We spent the night waiting for somebody to come back with a key.”  Brandon: “I'm sorry that happened.”

Panel 3 — MEDIUM past Eva's shoulder: Isabella looks at Brandon, anger becoming more personal. Do not stage an objective flashback showing Merritt at the crackdown. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Isabella: “You said we'd be safe.”  Brandon: “I didn't say that to you.”
Panel 4 — SMALL silent on Jessie watching the people who heard Isabella; a patron removes a coat as though deciding not to leave. NO LETTERING.

title: People Who Were There
summary: Different Mirage regulars have their own memories of the crackdown, and none is introduced as a definitive narrator answer.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — WIDE from stage side: Marta brings a glass of water and puts it by Isabella without choosing the center of the dispute. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Marta: “Sit down. Your legs are shaking.”  Isabella: “They're fine.”  Marta: “Sit anyway.”

Panel 2 — MEDIUM on Len sitting on an overturned music case near the table, leaving space for Isabella. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Len: “Nobody knew who was coming back that night.”  Isabella: “I knew who promised.”

Panel 3 — TIGHT on a patron at the far table, an ordinary older regular who can still hear; half the group is deliberately ignoring the drama. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Older patron: “Some of us stopped waiting.”  Isabella: “I didn't.”

Panel 4 — QUIET close of Brandon looking down briefly, not as if he remembers Merritt's life but because Isabella is upset. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: CAPTION: “The old trouble belonged to the people who had lived through it. Brandon knew none of them.”

title: What She Needed to Say
summary: Brandon stops debating the mistaken identity long enough to give Isabella room to address Merritt's absence. This is a human exchange, not therapy or a political verdict.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — MEDIUM table with clearer personal distance: Isabella sits; Brandon remains in the same chair, Jessie and Eva farther away, food growing cold. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Brandon: “What did you need to say to Merritt?”

Panel 2 — CLOSE Isabella struggling to say the thing she rehearsed privately; not posed as a villain. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Isabella: “That he left us here. That we were still here after the doors opened.”
Panel 3 — TIGHT reverse on Brandon, listening. He does not claim he understands her history. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Brandon: “Then say it. I'll listen.”

Panel 4 — TALL on Isabella making direct eye contact; people behind drift back to eating. Her anger has not vanished. EXACT SCRIPTED LETTERING: Isabella: “He always thought coming back later was the same as staying.”  Brandon: “I can't answer for him.”

title: At the End of the Hall
summary: Isabella brings Eva and Jessie toward a side corridor and introduces the preacher lead without overexplaining it.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — TALL club geography: Isabella leads Eva through the short side corridor behind the stage. Jessie follows; Brandon stays seated at the table in the background with the food Marta brought. The stair to street remains across the room.
